LESSON: ARABIC ALPHABET

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: QUR’AN
Topic 1.1: Arabic alphabet

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Arabic alphabet. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya
3. practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps
4. apply Arabic alphabet in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ARABIC ALPHABET
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Arabic alphabet helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ARABIC ALPHABET
Study Arabic alphabet like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Arabic alphabet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Arabic alphabet in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Arabic alphabet in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Arabic alphabet in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Arabic alphabet in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Arabic alphabet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Arabic alphabet in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Arabic alphabet is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Arabic alphabet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Arabic alphabet in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Arabic alphabet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Arabic alphabet in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Arabic alphabet to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Arabic alphabet in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Arabic alphabet from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Arabic alphabet: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Arabic alphabet?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Arabic alphabet means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Arabic alphabet means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Arabic alphabet from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
